@@ -13,7 +13,7 @@ The fire. Ember grass is back on a burn within days and dries to tinder soon aft
 
 The weather. Fine ash drifts through the air like snow even on clear days. Ash fall and cinderfall bank loose ash across the map, and cinderfall brings lightning with it. The only rain is black rain: a short, filthy downpour that puts fires out, washes the loose ash away and waters the ash beneath, so a burn it falls on grows faster still.
 
-Behind the fire, some solace. A scorch-fruit pod appears only where flame has just cracked one open and rots within a day, so the harvest happens during the burn or not at all. A firefoam sprayer lets you decide where the next burn stops. Pyrelands sand can be shovelled for glass sand, leaving gravel behind, so every sand patch is a finite deposit.
+Fire pays. A scorch-fruit pod appears only where flame has just cracked one open and rots within a day, so the harvest happens during the burn or not at all. A firefoam sprayer lets you decide where the next burn stops. Pyrelands sand can be shovelled for glass sand, leaving gravel behind, so every sand patch is a finite deposit.
 
 The creatures. The fire-hawk carries a live ember away to start a new burn. The giant furnace-beast warms the ground around it, banks heat in the burn and smoulders the bed it lies in. Ullai herds drift to wherever it burned a couple of days ago. The ashwallow goes to ground ahead of a fire front and curls into its dome when struck by heat. The emberscythe mantis, sytheclaw, barbslinger with its tail spikes, venomous flamefang and fire wasp round out the cast.
